rv.q: Uneven drama examines themes of abuse, complicity and resilience from the perspective of interned historian Hannah Arendt

But the country all the women loved was now gone beneath the jackboot, slicing off the greater part of their German-Jewish identity. You can see the thoughts that led to her later works formulating in real time, especially in her reaction to the hate exhibited by the French peasantry near the camp.

In addition to the pain that dominates the story, there is uncanny humour sprinkled throughout. Humour in the face of suffering incites breaths of relief from the audience while adding complexity to the characters. Pascal achieves nuance for the most part, allowing space for contradictions to be true at the same time without lecturing.
